title: Acme Logistics, in three levels
subtitle: Who uses it, what runs, and what is inside the API.

verdict.text: Acme Logistics books, tracks and invoices parcels for counter staff, through an Angular web app, a .NET API that holds the business rules, a Python tracking worker, PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ. A change is most likely to hurt around delivery: the API and the worker can both mark a shipment delivered, but only the API's `/delivered` endpoint issues an invoice, and nothing in this repository calls it. [high]

sections.title: The system
sections.intro: Start at Context and move to Containers, then Inside the API. Click a box for its card. The three requests play at the Containers level. Marked links are where to be careful.

boxes.label: Counter staff
details: Use the web app at the counters. `README.md:9` [high]

boxes.label: Depot / back office
details: Six API endpoints have no screen and no caller in this repository: read one shipment, mark delivered, cancel, read tracking, reweigh and credit. Commit messages mention reweighing at the depot and credit notes, so I assume staff or a tool outside this repository call them. [guess]
Marking delivered is the only path that issues an invoice. [high]

boxes.label: Customer
details: Receives the `parcel-delivered` message. The code calls this person the customer and does not say whether that is the sender or the recipient. `worker/src/acme_worker/notifications.py:1` [high]

boxes.label: Carrier API
details: The delivery partner that knows a parcel's position and status. [high]
The worker sends a GET to `ACME_CARRIER_URL` plus the shipment id, with a 10 s timeout. `worker/src/acme_worker/tracking.py:19` [high]
The worker raises an error and the API's tracking request answers 500. Booking and invoicing are not touched. [med]
Which carrier this is: the only address in the repository is a placeholder. [guess]

boxes.label: Notification API
details: Tells the customer that a parcel has arrived. [high]

The worker sends a POST to `ACME_NOTIFY_URL` with the template `parcel-delivered` and a 5 s timeout. The Compose file does not set this setting, so the default in the code applies. `worker/src/acme_worker/notifications.py:7` [high]
The status is already Delivered. The worker raises before reporting to the API, so the API's tracking request answers 500. The next tracking request sends the message again. [med]
Which provider this is and which channel it uses. [guess]

boxes.label: Acme Logistics
details: Parcel delivery software for businesses in and around Novi Sad: booking, pricing, tracking and invoicing. `README.md:3` [high]
The two briefs in `docs/briefs/` describe future systems. Nothing from them is drawn. [high]

boxes.label: Web app
details: Shipment list, a Book button with a price estimate, and invoice lookup by shipment. It makes three API calls. `web/src/app/api/client.ts:35-45` [high]
No data. A second copy of the price rules in `web/src/app/shipments/pricing.ts:10-33`. [high]
The counters cannot book or look up invoices, while the API keeps running. API errors are not shown to staff, because the calls have no error handler. `web/src/app/shipments/shipments.ts:44` [high]

boxes.label: API
details: Ten HTTP endpoints for shipments and invoices, and every rule about price, status and invoicing. The rules are in the library `Acme.Logistics`, which runs inside this process. [high]
Tables `parcels` and `invoices` and the sequence `invoice_numbers`. It shares `shipments` with the worker. [high]
Booking, invoicing and tracking all stop. There is no error handling, so a broken rule such as an empty recipient answers 500 rather than 400. [med]
No login or access check of any kind, and Compose publishes port 8080. [high]

boxes.label: Tracking worker
boxes.note: Asks the carrier about a parcel, on request.
details: Answers `POST /track`: asks the carrier, records a delivery, notifies the customer and reports back to the API. It also consumes `shipment.booked`, but only writes a log line. [high]
The queue `worker.booked`. No table of its own, but it writes `shipments.status` directly. [high]
The API's tracking request answers 500, while booking and invoicing continue. If the consumer thread dies, the HTTP server keeps running and nothing restarts the thread. [high]
No timer or polling. The carrier is asked only when a tracking request arrives. [high]

boxes.label: Database
details: The one durable store, used by both the API and the worker. [high]
Tables `shipments`, `parcels` and `invoices`, and the sequence `invoice_numbers`. Sender, recipient and address are personal data. [high]
The API and the tracking writes stop, and their callers get 500. [med]
No table definitions or migrations in the repository, and no named volume in Compose. [high]

boxes.label: Message broker
details: Carries four shipment events from the API on the topic exchange `acme.events`. Only `shipment.booked` reaches a queue in this repository. [high]

On booking, the shipment is saved and the request still answers 500, so trying again makes a second booking. On delivery, the status is saved and no invoice is issued until someone repeats the call. The retry covers only the send, not the connection. `src/Acme.Logistics/Infrastructure/MessageBus.cs:20-25` [high]

boxes.label: Controllers
details: Turn HTTP requests into service calls and shape the JSON answers. `Program.cs` wires the parts together. [high]
An unhandled error from any service answers 500. [med]

boxes.label: Shipments
details: Validates and books shipments, moves them between statuses, calls the worker for tracking and publishes events. [high]
The status rules of a shipment, and the limits of 70 kg and 180 cm. [high]
Delivery runs as three separate steps with no transaction: status, event, invoice. A failure after the first leaves a Delivered shipment with no invoice. [high]

boxes.label: Pricing rules
details: Price from weight or volumetric weight, with surcharges for heavy, express, remote zone and fuel. [high]
The eight numbers behind the price. The same eight are repeated in the web app, so a change must be made in both. [high]
A plain calculation with no outside calls. [high]

boxes.label: Billing
details: Issues an invoice for a delivered shipment, lists invoices and marks one credited. Billing and Shipments depend on each other, so neither can change alone. [high]
No check in the code stops a second invoice if delivery is called twice. Whether the database does is unknown, because its schema is not in the repository. [med]

boxes.label: Domain
details: Money with its currency, and a parcel's size and weight. [high]
Table `parcels`, through `Parcel.ReweighAsync`, which writes SQL from inside the domain model. [high]
A failed reweigh leaves the stored weight unchanged. The price is not recalculated in any case. [high]

boxes.label: Persistence
details: Opens a connection per call and runs the SQL for shipments. [high]
Database errors go straight up to the caller, with no retry. [high]

boxes.label: Event publisher
details: Opens a new broker connection for each event and publishes it to `acme.events`. [high]
The event format: JSON with a routing key. [high]
If the broker cannot be reached, the error goes up to the caller. [high]

boxes.label: Common helpers
details: Date format, text cleaning, adding VAT and a simple retry. [high]
The VAT rate of 20%, which is a business rule kept in a general helper file. [high]
Plain functions with no outside calls. [high]

blocks.title: What a newcomer should know first
items: **Delivery has two writers and one invoice path.** The API and the worker both set a shipment to Delivered, but only the API's `/delivered` endpoint issues an invoice, and nothing here calls it. [high]

**The worker does not follow parcels on its own.** It has no timer and its queue consumer only logs. The carrier is asked only when something calls the API's tracking endpoint, and nothing here does. [high]
**Tracking is a loop.** One request goes from the API to the worker and the carrier, and back into the API before the first request is answered, so each needs the other to be up. [high]
**A broker outage can lose an invoice.** At delivery the status is saved, the event fails and no invoice is issued until someone repeats the call, because the steps share no transaction. [high]
**The price rules live in two places.** `PricingRules.cs` and `pricing.ts` hold the same eight numbers, and each pricing change so far was made in both by hand. [high]
**Nothing is protected.** The API and the worker have no login or access check and both publish a port, and the Compose file holds the database and broker passwords in plain text. [high]

blocks.title: Assumptions I made
items: The part that matters most is the API: pricing, the shipment status rules and all invoicing are in it, so it is the container opened here. The worker is described in its card.
Docker Compose is the deployment, because it is the only deployment description in the repository.
Someone outside this repository calls the six API endpoints that have no screen. They are drawn as one box, Depot / back office. [guess]
The carrier and the notification service are real, separate systems, although the addresses in the repository are placeholders. [guess]
The two briefs in `docs/briefs/` are future systems, so nothing from them is drawn.
Everything comes from reading commit 432aa50. Nothing was built or run, so failure behaviour marked [med] is read from the code and not observed.

blocks.title: Questions to settle
items: Who calls `POST /api/shipments/{id}/delivered`? It is the only path to an invoice and nothing here calls it. Ask this first. [high]
Should a delivery reported by the carrier issue an invoice? Today it sets Delivered and no invoice follows. [high]
Who listens to `shipment.delivered`, `shipment.tracked` and `shipment.reweighed`? No queue in this repository receives them, so unless something outside binds one, the broker drops them. [med]

Where is the database schema? The repository has no table definitions or migrations, and no code inserts into `parcels`, although every shipment read joins to it. As written, a new shipment could not be read back unless something else adds that row. [med]
How does the browser reach the API? The web app calls relative `/api` paths, and the repository has no proxy setting, `angular.json` or Angular entry file. [high]
Does the booking page work as committed? Its template has no input fields, so it can only send the default values, and the API refuses an empty recipient. [high]
Should reweighing change the price? Today it changes only the stored weight. `ShipmentService.cs:141-151` [high]
How does the carrier know our shipment? The worker asks by internal shipment id, and nothing in this repository registers a parcel with the carrier. [high]
